seven_q.Q0_posture: This document takes a structural, formal, and analytical stance — it treats theological and mathematical domains as isomorphic structures to be mapped precisely.
seven_q.Q1_identity: An isomorphism record (ISO-002) that maps six impossibility theorems from mathematics/physics to five properties of grace from Christian theology.
seven_q.Q2_domain: Lives at the intersection of mathematics, physics, philosophy, and Christian theology — a structural isomorphism between formal impossibility results and soteriological necessity.
seven_q.Q3_claim: Closed systems are structurally incapable of self-rescue (six theorems), and grace as described in Ephesians 2:8-9 has exactly the five properties (externality, sufficiency, asymmetric cost, merit-independence, temporal priority) that any external rescue must have to overcome these impossibilities.
seven_q.Q4_support: Six independent theorems from mathematics and physics (Gödel, Tarski, Turing, Clausius, Landauer, Leibniz), each rigorously proven and independently strengthened over centuries, plus the swap test confirming one-to-one mapping.
seven_q.Q5_dependencies: Depends on the validity of the six theorems, the theological definition of grace in Ephesians 2:8-9, and the structural isomorphism methodology established in ISO-001.
seven_q.Q6_consequences: Forces the conclusion that Pelagianism and semi-Pelagianism are structurally incoherent; any coherent soteriology must have all five grace properties; the Reformation debate maps to the coupling coefficient α(u); closed-system AI alignment is Gödelian-constrained.
seven_q.Q7_kill: Breaking any single theorem (e.g., finding a closed system that proves its own consistency) removes the necessity of the corresponding grace property; breaking all six eliminates the structural necessity for grace entirely.
